ASSEMBLY
1 Front module slides UP into the dome's side grooves from below. Nothing retains it at this point.
2 It seats against the lip; 4.5 mm of its edge is captured all round, with 0.5 sliding clearance.
3 Bottom plate goes on. Its top face is the module's datum - the module's bottom edge lands on it and can no longer drop.
4 Six M3 screws pull the bottom plate up into the dome bosses. No fastener touches the facade.
NOTES
a ONE FRONT PIECE, YES - but the diffuser stays separate. You cannot print an even diffuser; the printed part is the frame and
the cavity, and the Glowforge-cut opal acrylic drops into a pocket from behind. Everything that must stay in register with
everything else - matrix aperture, grilles, mic ports, diffuser - is now on ONE part, so there are no stacked tolerances.
b The facade went 3 -> 4 mm. Two 45x50 sealed boxes on an unsupported 3 mm plate will flex and buzz; it is a baffle now, not a cover.
Ribs run from each baffle ring out to the perimeter for the same reason.
c AIR GAP IS A GUESS. 12 mm is ~0.7x the 16.5 mm LED pitch, the usual starting point for not seeing 48 dots through opal.
Test-print the crescent corner before committing - this is the one number most likely to need changing.
d FIXINGS ARE WALL LUGS, NOT FLOOR BOSSES. Each lug is a pad that projects inward off the dome wall with a blind heat-set hole; the
screw comes up through the bottom plate and grabs it. Lugs live at the perimeter where the plate needs support anyway, and they
cost no floor area - which matters, because the floor is fully spoken for. Clearances per lug are in the key beside the plan.
e NO LUG ON THE FRONT EDGE. The speaker bodies own both front corners and the matrix owns the middle, so there is nowhere to put one.
It does not need one: the plate's front edge is captured between the seating ledge and the front module's bottom edge.
f TPA2016 moved to the REAR WALL at y=4. There is no floor left for it, and the speaker leads are shortest from there.
Bridge-tied outputs: do NOT common the two speakers' negatives (HARDWARE.md).
g SPEAKERS HANG ON NUBS, TOP AND BOTTOM, not on a baffle bolt pattern. The bodies are ROTATED 90 deg, so the two nubs -- one centred on each 50 mm face -- point UP and DOWN.
The module carries a POST above and below each body, on its vertical CENTRELINE, 10 x 6, standing 7 proud of the back face, with an M3 front-to-back into it.
THE FLANKS CARRY NOTHING. Two screws on one vertical line fix x, y and rotation between them, so there are no seat rings and no side ribs -- the width chain budgets
SPK_FLANK 1 mm per flank as pure clearance and it butts straight onto the dome's rib keep-out, so anything there jams the module on assembly.
NUB PROJECTION IS A GUESS (4 mm). Rotated, it now costs HEIGHT, not width: 6 mm at each end of the body. SPK_NUB_H (6) sets the post WIDTH,
which is what keeps it clear of the mic array by 9.9 mm and lets the array sit 3 mm above the body instead of above the post. Measure both before you print.
h THE TWO MATRICES ARE ONLY LOOSELY SOLDERED TOGETHER, so the frame cannot treat them as one part. Each board is located by its OWN two posts through its
own Ø2 diagonal holes, seats on two pads in the clear margin above and below its LED field, and the pair is clamped by SIX clips - two on
each long edge and one at each end. There is no tray and no pocket: a pocket would locate the PAIR, and the pair is exactly the thing that is not rigid.
The clock aperture is ONE OPEN 84 x 23 rectangle - no per-pixel holes. Through a 4 mm facade a per-pixel tunnel would kill the viewing angle.
